name: Crucible for Plex
subtitle: Native client for your server
promotionalText: Your library, native on iPhone, iPad and Apple TV: a Resume-first Home, the system player, offline downloads and a Year in Review. No server? Try the built-in demo.
description:
Crucible is a native client for your Plex Media Server on iPhone, iPad and Apple TV. It is built to feel like part of the system: the system player, native menus and context menus, Liquid Glass on the newest software, and a library that opens exactly where you left off.

PICK UP WHERE YOU LEFT OFF
Home opens on a Resume hero, then Continue Watching, Up Next and Recently Added. Library grids have filters for Unwatched and In Progress, genre and sort, an A–Z scrubber and folder browsing for unindexed content. Search groups results by type with a Top Result.

A PLAYER THAT RESPECTS YOUR TIME
Skip Intro and Skip Credits from Plex markers, audio and subtitle menus, adjustable speed, lock screen controls and Up Next that rolls the next episode as the credits start and carries on through the end of a season. On iPhone and iPad: Picture-in-Picture and background audio. Direct play when your device can handle the file, automatic transcoding when it can't.

MADE FOR IPAD
A sidebar with every Plex library, layouts that fit every window from Slide Over to a full 13-inch screen, and several windows at once: open any title in its own window from its menu, or drag its card to the edge of the screen. With a Magic Keyboard, a full menu bar and shortcuts: Command-1 to 4 for the tabs, Command-F to search, Space to play, S to skip the intro, N for the next episode. Posters lift under the trackpad and Apple Pencil, and right-click opens every menu.

MADE FOR THE COUCH
The Apple TV app is built for the Siri Remote: a cinematic Home that follows focus, one tab per library, native context menus, search, and Top Shelf with Continue Watching and Up Next. Liquid Glass on tvOS 26.

TAKE IT OFFLINE
On iPhone and iPad, download movies, seasons or single episodes in the quality you pick. Transfers continue in the background, stay on Wi-Fi by default and, on iPhone, show a Live Activity on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island. Offline playback uses the same player.

KNOW YOUR VIEWING
Watch History grouped by day, Statistics with streaks, heatmaps, binges and taste built from your own Plex history, and a Year in Review poster you can share.

FREE TO USE, CRUCIBLE PRO TO GO FURTHER
Browsing, search and playback are free on iPhone, iPad and Apple TV, and so is the Statistics view for the last week. Crucible Pro unlocks unlimited offline downloads, the full Statistics screen with every range and library filter, the Year in Review poster and Top Shelf. Pay once for lifetime access, or subscribe yearly. One purchase covers iPhone, iPad and Apple TV, and Family Sharing is on.

TRY IT WITHOUT A SERVER
No Plex server yet? Choose Try the demo on the welcome screen to explore a fictional library with everything unlocked, guided by a short tour.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No sign-up, no ads, no analytics. Crucible talks to plex.tv and the server you choose, and records Crucible Pro purchases with an anonymous Midgar ID, with no sign-up.

OPEN SOURCE
Crucible is free software under GPL-3.0: https://github.com/guitaripod/Crucible

Crucible needs a Plex Media Server. Plex requires a Plex Pass or Remote Watch Pass to stream from your server away from home. Crucible is an independent app and is not made by, endorsed by or affiliated with Plex, Inc. Plex is a trademark of Plex, Inc.

Crucible Pro Annual: billed yearly at the price shown in the app. The subscription renews automatically unless you cancel at least 24 hours before the end of the period. Manage it in your Apple Account settings.
Terms of Use (EULA): https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/dev/stdeula/
Privacy Policy: https://midgarcorp.cc/crucible/privacy
reviewNotes:
WHAT CHANGED FOR THE 2.1(a) REVIEW
- The built-in demo now shows every account type, so no credentials are needed (steps below).
- Closing the Plex sign-in sheet used to leave the Welcome screen busy for minutes with "Try the demo" greyed out; it now comes back at once.

Crucible is a client for the user's own Plex Media Server and has no content of its own. Plex requires a paid Plex Pass or Remote Watch Pass to stream a server's video away from home (https://support.plex.tv/articles/requirements-for-remote-playback-of-personal-media/), so we cannot give App Review a working account and server. The demo runs a fictional Plex server inside the app instead (Guideline 2.1(a)): no account, server or network needed, on iPhone, iPad and Apple TV alike.

START THE DEMO
On the Welcome screen tap "Try the demo" (below "Sign in with Plex"), then "Start exploring". Everything below is under the You tab.

ACCOUNT TYPES IN THE DEMO
1. Server owner (the demo starts as "Demo"): every feature unlocked, plus the owner's tools: Manage in a title's menu (Fix Match, Edit Details, poster and background, Delete, scans), Stop Stream in Server Activity, Server Dashboard under You.
2. Plex Home member with a PIN: You > Switch Profile > Sam, PIN 1234. Sam has a watch history of their own and no owner tools.
3. Managed (restricted) profile: You > Switch Profile > Kids, no PIN. Only family titles appear. Switch Profile > Demo returns to the owner.
4. Free install and Crucible Pro: the demo starts unlocked. Turn on You > Preview Free Version to see a free install: Statistics ranges past Week, the Statistics library filter, the Year in Review poster and more than one download are locked and open the paywall. A purchase there (sandbox) unlocks them for real; Restore Purchases is on the paywall.
5. Pro Week: with Preview Free Version on, watch any title to the end (demo titles are 30-second clips) and close the player: a free week of Pro starts and is announced, and Settings > Crucible Pro counts down its days. The demo's week is separate from the device's.

CRUCIBLE PRO (in-app purchases, StoreKit with Midgar's own engine, MidgarKit)
com.guitaripod.crucible.pro.lifetime, non-consumable, $17.99 (rises to $24.99 on December 7, 2026); com.guitaripod.crucible.pro.yearly, auto-renewable, $7.99 a year, no free trial. Both approved; Apple TV shares them through universal purchase. Playback is never gated. Paywall: Settings > Crucible Pro, the end of the demo tour, or any lock in the free preview.

ALSO IN 2.7.2 (since 2.4.0, the last iPhone release; all of it works in the demo)
The Pro Week, half-star ratings, collections, playlists, cast filmographies, trailers and extras, library filters, subtitle search, the Plex watchlist, titles offered when a movie ends, Autoplay Next Episode at the credits, searchable Settings, sleep timer, chapters, Stream Info, quality per network, languages remembered per show, live Home and Server Activity, one gathered rating reminder. Notifications for new episodes and watchlist arrivals follow changes on a real server, which the fixed demo library never has; a rating reminder (finish a title, then leave the app) shows the same notification flow in the demo.

OTHER NOTES
Sign in with Plex uses plex.tv's own web sign-in; an account with no server is pointed to the demo. Downloads save media from the user's own server for offline viewing inside the app. Local network access is requested to reach servers on the user's home network; App Transport Security allows arbitrary loads because Plex servers on private addresses use HTTP or self-signed HTTPS. No third-party SDK; the only data is an anonymous Midgar ID (iCloud Keychain) for Crucible Pro purchases, as the privacy policy and App Privacy answers describe.

whatsNew.IOS:
A week of Crucible Pro, on us: watch a film or episode to the end and unlimited downloads, every Statistics range, the Year in Review poster and Top Shelf on Apple TV are open for seven days, once per device. Nothing to sign up for and nothing is charged.

Crucible now speaks German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Brazilian Portuguese, and Simplified and Traditional Chinese, on iPhone, iPad and Apple TV. Statistics also show your busiest hour in your device's clock format.

More of Plex, on iPhone, iPad and Apple TV.

- When a movie or the last episode of a show ends, titles like it wait on screen; pick a movie and it plays right away
- Autoplay Next Episode now starts the next episode at the credits on its own, on Apple TV too
- Switch between the profiles of your Plex Home, with their PIN
- Home, Server Activity and the Server Dashboard update live as your server changes
- Rate any title in half stars, sort a library by Your Rating, and rate what you just watched from Home
- Build playlists from any title's menu, then play or shuffle them
- Browse collections, open a cast member's titles, and watch trailers and extras
- Filter a library by decade, age rating and resolution, and search for subtitles online
- Keep your Plex watchlist under You
- Rating reminders and notifications for new episodes, watchlist arrivals, a weekly recap and Year in Review (iPhone and iPad)
- One rating reminder gathers everything you finished and opens Rate What You Watched, a list with stars on every row (iPhone and iPad)
- Libraries you switch off in Settings now stay out of search, suggestions, rating reminders and notifications too, not only Home and Statistics
- Settings rebuilt as searchable categories, plus Home Rows to arrange Home
- A sleep timer, chapters, Stream Info, quality for home, away and cellular, and languages remembered per show
- For server owners: Manage titles and libraries (Fix Match, Edit Details, artwork, Show Settings, scans), stop a stream, and a Server Dashboard
- The demo now shows every kind of account: switch to a Plex Home profile with a PIN or to a managed Kids profile, or preview the free version with Crucible Pro locked
- Closing the Plex sign-in now brings you straight back to the welcome screen
- Crucible now moves between your home network, Tailscale and remote connections on its own as you come and go, picks a playing stream back up on the new connection, and lets you choose a connection in Server & Connection
whatsNew.TV_OS: Fixed the row of filters at the top of a library: when it holds more buttons than fit on the screen, as it does for a server owner, it now scrolls sideways as you move along it, so every button keeps its full name and the remote reaches each one.
